title: a-charter-may-not-assert-a-file-that-is-not-there
intention: A charter's present-tense claim about a file at its own address is checked against the address. Two halves, and the second is what makes the first stay true: (1) the seven chart-machine charters that assert 'state.json + history.json beside this charter. Both were born at the carve-out' are corrected to say what is true — the journal is born at this address's FIRST CROSSING, and until a ticket crosses here there is none; (2) the check that reds a charter naming a file beside it that is not there lands as a BUILD_INSPECTOR SIEVE — fired at every PROVEME crossing by physics — with bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate carrying the same predicate as the hand-run surface, so the next charter written by copying a sibling cannot inherit the falsehood silently.
why:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, and the measurement is small and total. Eight machines sit under cairn/devices/builder/machines/. Seven of their charters state in the present tense that state.json and history.json sit beside them; at seven of those seven, NEITHER FILE EXISTS. The eighth is orient, and its files did not exist either until this morning, when the orient-floor ticket crossed BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME -> PROVED and read_history's tolerance for an absent file created them on first append.

So the sentence is false twice over, and the second falsehood is the one that matters. It is not merely that the files are missing — the MECHANISM the sentence names is wrong. 'Born at the carve-out' describes a birth that has never happened at any of the eight addresses. What actually births a journal is a crossing, which is why orient's arrived weeks after its carve-out and the other seven's have not arrived at all. A reader trusting the charter would go looking for a record of the carve-out voyages and find nothing, and would have no way to tell whether the record was lost or was never written.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a Cairn mind stands in constrain/ to be briefed, reads that the machine's history is beside it, opens the directory, and finds no history. It now has to work out from first principles whether it is looking at a broken component, a lost record, or a component that has simply never sailed — and it has to do that at every one of the seven. That is Law 1's defect exactly: re-deriving a settled answer, seven times, because the artifact that should have carried it says something else.

WHY THE FIX IS NOT 'CREATE THE FILES'. An empty state.json at constrain would make the sentence true and the corpus worse: it manufactures a record of a voyage that did not happen, which is what Law 7 exists to forbid. The absence is HONEST. The charter is what is wrong.
traces_to: Law 5 — intent, its voyage, and its proofs share an address. A charter that misdescribes what is at its own address is the drift Law 5 is built to make impossible.
Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. 'Do not assert a file that is not there' is prose in this ticket and stays a tracked debt until the derivation gate carries it.
Law 9 — red is the default. Seven charters currently read green about their own address because nothing derives the claim.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. The eight-address census is the measurement; before it, the claim was believed because it appeared in seven files.

falsifier.proves_green: (1) The seven charters no longer assert a journal that is not there. What they say instead is a claim about the mechanism — the journal is born at the first crossing at this address — and it is TRUE of all eight, including orient, whose files arrived exactly that way. (2) The predicate — walk a charter, extract the filenames it asserts sit beside it, red any that is absent — lands as a build_inspector sieve, so it fires at EVERY PROVEME crossing without anyone remembering to run it (Law 4). bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate carries the same predicate for the hand-run corpus sweep; the sieve is the physics and the gate check is the surface. (3) The predicate reds TODAY on a deliberately malformed fixture and goes green on the corpus after (1) — a check that could only ever pass is the hollow build Law 8 refuses.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) any of the seven charters still asserts state.json or history.json beside it while the file is absent; (2) the correction is made by creating empty journals rather than by correcting the sentence — that is manufacturing a record of a voyage that never sailed; (3) the new gate check passes on a fixture that asserts a file which is not there; (4) the check is written to look only for state.json and history.json — the defect is a charter asserting ANY file beside it, and narrowing it to the two filenames that happened to be wrong today is fitting the instrument to the sample; (5) the corrected sentence claims the journal will be born at the first crossing without that being true of orient, the one case where it can be checked against a real history.
falsifier.horizon: After the chart floor build order Akien set on 2026-08-14 — orient, then constrain, then survey. This ticket was found WHILE building orient's floor and is deliberately not being fixed inside that build; but constrain and survey are two of the seven, so their charters are corrected as those stages are built, and the gate check lands with survey at the latest. Waiting past that means writing two more charters from a template known to be wrong.

chart_notes.orient: The seven charters are cairn/devices/builder/machines/{constrain,decompose,hypothesize,survey,triage,validate,verdict}/intention+why.json, field state_and_history. The gate is bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate, whose checks live beside the map derivation; it currently proves eight over 54 charters. orient's journal, the one working example, is at cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/{state,history}.json.
